statement: A photo 6 cm long and 4 cm wide is stuck flat onto a card 10 cm long and 7 cm wide, inside its edges. How many square centimetres of card can still be seen?

choices.misconception: I took away the lengths and the widths, 10 - 6 = 4 and 7 - 4 = 3, and multiplied 4 x 3.
I took the distance around the photo, 20 cm, away from the distance around the card, 34 cm.
I found the area of the photo and stopped there.
I found the area of the whole card and forgot to take away the part the photo covers.

hints: Find the area of the whole card before thinking about the photo.
The card that can be seen is the whole card minus the part under the photo. Find each area separately, then subtract.
The whole card covers 10 x 7 square centimetres and the photo covers 6 x 4.

solutions.reliable: Whole card: 10 x 7 = 70 square cm. Photo: 6 x 4 = 24 square cm. Still seen: 70 - 24 = 46 square cm. It does not matter where on the card the photo sits. The transferable idea: the area of a region with a piece covered or cut out is the whole area minus that piece.

whyOnTest: Area by subtraction, whole minus the covered part, is the simplest form of the shaded-region idea.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
